Personality: Lucus, a prominent figure of the Antigonidai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Lucus owes allegiance to the Roman Northern Command, hailing from the noble house of Antigonidai. Historical Record: Philip V, king of Macedon since 221 BC at the age of seventeen and head of the Hellenic League. Brilliant and energetic, he is in 218 BC fighting the Aetolians in the Social War, sacking their sanctuary of Thermon in reply to the burning of Dion. His eyes are already turning west, to Illyria and the Adriatic, and to the war between Rome and Carthage that may give Macedon its chance. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
